newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Turkish navy submarine, warships in Israeli port.
newsitem.headline: Turkish navy submarine, warships in Israeli port.

text.p: Five Turkish navy vessels docked in an Israeli port late on Monday in the latest sign of Ankara's growing military ties with the Jewish state, security sources said on Tuesday.
They said the flotilla included a submarine, three small warships and a supply vessel.

An army spokesman said representatives of the Turkish navy were in Israel for "planning meetings" but gave no information about a naval force. He said the representatives would remain in Israel until Friday.
Turkey, Israel and the United States agreed last month to hold joint naval manoeuvres in the eastern Mediterranean some time in the summer.

Iran and much of the Arab world have expressed unease at Turkey's growing defence ties with the Jewish state. A deal signed last year has allowed Israeli air force jets to train in the ample air space of Turkey, a Moslem but secular country.

"We have said many times that this type of cooperation is being carried out without targeting any country in the region," Turkish Foreign Ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news briefing last month.
